title: Nasal spray live attenuated influenza vaccine: the first experience in Italy in children and adolescents during the 2020-21 season.
ehr_evidence: A questionnaire was given out to parents on the day of the vaccination, on a voluntary and anonymous basis, through which information about children and their parents was collected.
summary: Observational study evaluating the safety, adverse events, and parental satisfaction of the first use of nasal quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine (qLAIV) in Italian children and adolescents aged 2-17 years during the 2020-21 season.
key_findings: Adverse events were reported in 24.8% of children (80.6% mild, 18.1% moderate, 1.3% significant).
Most common adverse events were cold/rhinitis (52.5%) and fever (24.4%).
Children aged 2-5 years had an increased risk of adverse events compared to 6-10 years (aRR 1.7, 95% CI 1.5-1.9, p<0.001) and 11-17 years (aRR 1.5, 95% CI 1-2.2, p=0.051).
Children with at least one acute infectious disease in 2020 had higher risk (aRR 1.2, 95% CI 1.1-1.4, p=0.004) and those with chronic diseases had higher risk (aRR 1.6, 95% CI 1.2-2.1, p=0.001).
Males had a decreased probability of adverse reactions compared to females (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-1, p=0.011).

No significant association was found between adverse events and prematurity (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.7-1.1, p=0.220), allergic diseases (aRR 1.1, 95% CI 0.7-1.5, p=0.667), or previous influenza vaccination (aRR 0.9, 95% CI 0.8-1.1, p=0.382).
83.3% of parents were very satisfied and 83.8% intended to re-vaccinate their children.
Adverse reactions were the main reason for not repeating vaccination (aRR 5.5, 95% CI 2.4-12.5, p<0.001).
captured_features: Demographic data (age, sex, birthplace, gestational age, siblings, daycare attendance)
Vaccination history (previous flu vaccine, chronic diseases, acute infectious diseases)
Adverse event type and severity (mild, moderate, significant)
Parental satisfaction and intention to re-vaccinate
population: children and adolescents aged 2-17 years in Milan, Italy
exposure_domain: influenza vaccination (quadrivalent live attenuated influenza vaccine)
limitations: self-reported data via questionnaires and phone calls
selection bias due to high proportion of university-educated parents and Italian nationality
telephone follow-up attrition (600 null questionnaires excluded)
